plan.title: Heart 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is whether the drug's transcriptional effect differs by genotype — a genotype x treatment interaction. The data is a 2x2 factorial (WT/KO x vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 16 samples used of 17 in the file — metadata lists 16 rows) of raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes) in human heart. The plan follows the grounded procedure: (1) QC on variance-stabilized counts to confirm sample structure and rule out an outlier or mislabel before any test is trusted; (2) a single PyDESeq2 model with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (WT, vehicle), testing the interaction coefficient first (does the drug effect differ by genotype?) and then the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, and within KO) so the interaction result can be interpreted; (3) ashr shrinkage of every contrast (a multi-coefficient contrast, so ashr rather than apeglm); (4) BH-FDR with independent filtering per contrast; (5) enrichment agent runs preranked GSEA (gseapy prerank, mirroring fgsea logic) on the Wald statistic per contrast against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, respecting the size window (15-500) and reporting the ranking-metric choice as required by the disputed rule; (6) a final report step assembles the interaction table (simple effects + interaction contrast side by side), fit diagnostics, and the reproducibility record. All scripts are Python per the user's constraint (pydeseq2, gseapy) — no R steps are used even though the knowledge base's default template names DESeq2/fgsea in R; the Python equivalents (pydeseq2, gseapy prerank) implement the same grounded methods.
